rows.en: “She was here until about three hours ago.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But she was here until about three hours ago."

rows.jp: 「なんか今日はなかなか遭遇できませんで」

ghs.en: Miki: "Today I just can't really run into her at all."

rows.jp: 情緒不安定だからかな。
「一人になりたかったのかも」
rows.en: “She might have wanted to be alone.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Maybe she just wanted to be alone."

rows.jp: そういえば豊が死んだ日か。今日は。
rows.en: Come to think of it, today was the anniversary of Yutaka’s death.

ghs.en: Which reminds me, the anniversary of the day that Yutaka died... is today.

rows.en: Oh. Of course... That explained it.

rows.jp: 「……ま、今日はそっとしておいてあげたら？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...well, how about leaving it at that for today?"
ghs.assessment: そっとしておく means leaving Kiri alone and not disturbing her. 'Leave it at that' means stop discussing or doing an unspecified matter and loses the person being spared.

rows.jp: 「というか霧っちになにかエロいことしましたね？」
rows.en: “Or rather, did you try something dirty with Kiri?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Or should I say, did you do something pervy to Kiricchi?"
ghs.assessment: The affectionate Japanese nickname is carried over without an English representation.

rows.jp: しようとしたことは確かだが。

ghs.en: Well, it's true that I was going to do it.
ghs.assessment: しようとした says he actually tried or attempted it. 'Was going to' can mean mere intention and weakens the completed attempt.

highlights.text: I was going to do it

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am a Love Gentleman I am!"

rows.jp: 「しようとしたけど、きついこと言われて引き下がった」
rows.en: “I tried, she tore me a new one, and I backed down.”

ghs.en: Miki: "You were going to, but you were told something harsh and were stopped."
ghs.assessment: Taichi admits in the first person that he tried but backed down after being told something harsh. The English labels Miki as speaker and changes the confession into her second-person account of his behavior.

highlights.text: Miki: "You were going to, but you were told something harsh and were stopped."

rows.jp: 弟子に見抜かれる師匠の図。
rows.en: Behold: the master, seen through by his pupil.

ghs.en: A master being seen through by his pupil (artist's impression).

rows.jp: 「まあ……俺がクレイジーだということを、言葉巧みに説明された」
rows.en: “Well... She offered an eloquent explanation of the fact that I’m crazy.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well... it was explained to me with skillful words how I am cray-zee."

ghs.assessment: The intended colloquial statement requires a subject and tag punctuation, such as 'Well, it's true, isn't it?'

rows.jp: 正直、ちょっと落ち込んだ。
rows.en: Honestly, it had depressed me a little.

ghs.en: Honestly, I was a bit depressed.

rows.jp: 「先輩は……優しいモードの時は、好きですよ？」
rows.en: “I... like you when you’re in gentle mode.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Senpai... when you're in Nice Guy mode, I love you, you know?"
ghs.assessment: The status address is left unexplained, and 優しいモード means his gentle or kind mode. 'Nice Guy' carries a distinct modern social stereotype not supplied by the source.

rows.jp: 「誉め殺しのつもりか。百戦錬磨のこの俺、たやすくはだまされないぞ！」
rows.en: “Trying to flatter me to death? I am a veteran of a hundred campaigns. You will not deceive me so easily!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Do you want to kill me with faint praise? I am a veteran of a hundred battles, it is no easy thing to deceive me!"
ghs.assessment: 誉め殺し means praising someone extravagantly to death or buttering them up, not faint praise. The English chooses nearly the opposite degree of praise.

rows.jp: 「めっちゃニヤけてるんですけど」
rows.en: “You are grinning from ear to ear.”

ghs.en: Miki: "But you're totally an effeminate fop with a catty grin."
ghs.assessment: Miki simply points out that he is grinning broadly. The English invents gendered and class-coded insults and attributes cattiness absent from the source.

highlights.text: an effeminate fop with a catty grin

ghs.assessment: 俺の正直者 jokingly praises his own honest reaction or face for betraying him. It does not reveal an abstract 'real identity.'

rows.jp: 「なぜ怒られながら求婚されるのだろう……」
rows.en: “Why am I being proposed to in an angry voice...?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Why a marriage proposal in the middle of being angry even..."
ghs.assessment: 怒られながら means while she is being yelled at or angrily proposed to. 'Being angry' instead makes Miki herself the one experiencing anger.

highlights.text: in the middle of being angry

rows.jp: 「霧ちんがいいって言ったら」

ghs.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains unexplained rather than represented in English.

rows.jp: 「でも一応、今の一筆したためてくれる？」
rows.en: “Could you put that last part in writing, just in case?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But, for the time being, could I perhaps have that in writing?"

rows.jp: 「……そういうところがダメなんですってば」
rows.en: “...That. That right there is your problem.”

ghs.en: Miki: "...that part of you is completely rotten I keep telling you."
ghs.assessment: ダメ says that this trait is what is wrong with him or why he is hopeless. 'Completely rotten' adds a much harsher moral judgment.
